mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent acceleration in INDPRO and a deceleration in GDPC1 over the same month indicates a supply-side shock where output growth lags industrial production, reducing corporate earnings visibility and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month AND GDPC1 < previous month (same month)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in HOUST for three consecutive months signals weakening housing demand, which negatively impacts construction and home-related consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL over two months signals a successful disinflationary tightening, which boosts risk sentiment and yields a positive S&P 500 return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous month AND CPIAUCSL < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above trend by more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > trend by >0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above 5% YoY for six consecutive months signals a surge in household savings, which typically precedes a reduction in consumer spending and ultimately leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5% YoY for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
